metadata.scientific_integrity_notice: This generator produces synthetic engineering fixtures for multimodal architectural benchmarking. Acoustic features are simulated using non-target clinical covariates and residual Gaussian noise. They do not represent real physical recordings of postpartum patients.

speech_rate_syllables_per_sec.definition: Total syllable count divided by total elapsed duration (N_syl / T_total), inclusive of pauses.
speech_rate_syllables_per_sec.mathematical_nature: Direct acoustic scalar generated from baseline prior + covariate shift + correlated residual Gaussian noise.

pause_ratio.definition: Total silent pause duration divided by total elapsed duration (T_pause / T_total).
pause_ratio.mathematical_nature: Direct acoustic scalar generated from baseline prior + covariate shift + correlated residual Gaussian noise.

speech_to_pause_ratio.clamping_bounds: derived (strictly positive: [3.86, 62.80] observed in training set)
speech_to_pause_ratio.mathematical_nature: Engineered non-linear transformation of speech_rate and pause_ratio. It is NOT an independent acoustic measurement.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: Voice acoustical measurement of the severity of major depression
verified_literature_studies.authors: Michael Cannizzaro, Brian Harel, Nicole Reilly, Phillip Chappell, Peter J. Snyder
verified_literature_studies.population: Adult outpatients with Major Depressive Disorder
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Speaking rate, total pause time, pitch variability
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Speaking rate correlated negatively with HDRS (r = -0.74, p < 0.05); pause duration positive trend (r = 0.67, p = 0.09)
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Very small sample (N=7); general adult depression, not postpartum.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: Voice acoustic measures of depression severity and treatment response collected via interactive voice response (IVR) technology
verified_literature_studies.authors: James C. Mundt, Peter J. Snyder, Michael S. Cannizzaro, Kara Chappie, Dayna S. Geralts
verified_literature_studies.population: Adult outpatients with Major Depressive Disorder starting pharmacotherapy
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Speaking rate, total pause time, pause frequency
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Treatment responders had significant increase in speech rate (F = 7.15, p = 0.01) and decrease in pause time (F = 9.82, p = 0.004); Cohen d approx 0.50 - 0.70
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Telephone bandwidth (8 kHz); structured reading/counting tasks; not perinatal.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: A review of depression and suicide risk assessment using speech analysis
verified_literature_studies.authors: Nicholas Cummins, Stefan Scherer, Jarek Krajewski, Sebastian Schnieder, Julien Epps, Thomas F. Quatieri
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Pause duration, pause ratio, speech rate, spectral features
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Depression associated with 20-50% increase in pauses and 10-25% reduction in speech rate; effect sizes d approx 0.35 - 0.75
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Review across heterogeneous tasks; no postpartum-specific meta-analysis.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: Automatic Behavior Descriptors for Psychological Disorder Analysis
verified_literature_studies.authors: Stefan Scherer, Giota Stratou, Mahmoud Mahmoud, Jill Boberg, Jonathan Gratch, Albert Rizzo, Louis-Philippe Morency
verified_literature_studies.population: Military veterans and community adults (DAIC-WOZ, PHQ-8)
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Syllable rate, pause duration, pause ratio
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Pause metrics correlated with PHQ-8 (r approx 0.25 - 0.35, p < 0.001); speech rate negatively correlated (r approx -0.22 - -0.32); Cohen d approx 0.45 - 0.65
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Virtual agent interviewer; high proportion of male veterans; not perinatal.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: Maternal touch and maternal child-directed speech: effects of depressed mood in the postnatal period
verified_literature_studies.authors: Eisquel Herrera, Nadja Reissland, John Shepherd
verified_literature_studies.population: Postpartum mothers (6 and 10 months postpartum, EPDS screened)
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Infant-directed speech affective and informative content
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Depressed mothers produced significantly fewer affect-salient speech utterances (F(1, 34) = 4.88, p = 0.034, partial eta^2 = 0.126, d approx 0.76)
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Infant-directed speech; behavioral coding of utterances, not micro-acoustic pause ratio or syllable rate.

verified_literature_studies.full_title: Depression Diagnoses and Fundamental Frequency-Based Acoustic Cues in Maternal Infant-Directed Speech
verified_literature_studies.authors: Lyndsay L. Porritt, Mason C. Zinser, Jo-Anne Bachorowski, Peter S. Kaplan
verified_literature_studies.population: Postpartum mothers of infants 4-12 months (SCID-diagnosed MDD vs controls)
verified_literature_studies.speech_features: Mean F0 and pitch range (delta F0)
verified_literature_studies.reported_result: Clinically depressed mothers showed significantly restricted pitch range (delta F0 approx 35 Hz reduction, p < 0.05, d approx 0.55)
verified_literature_studies.limitation: Measured pitch range, not speech rate or pause ratio; infant-directed speech.

scenario_1_current_configuration.description: Current high-noise baseline with heavy residual Gaussian variance.
scenario_1_current_configuration.physiological_bounds_plausibility: All values lie within physiological limits; no severe clamping occurs. However, residual noise accounts for 85-90% of total feature variance, placing the audio modality near the random guessing threshold.

scenario_2_conservative_evidence_informe.description: Conservative evidence-informed calibration matching small-to-moderate depression effect sizes (Cohen d ~ 0.40 - 0.45).
scenario_2_conservative_evidence_informe.physiological_bounds_plausibility: Excellent physiological plausibility. Zero clamping. Maintains substantial unexplained inter-individual acoustic variance while allowing clinical signal to emerge.

scenario_3_moderate_evidence_informed.description: Moderate evidence-informed calibration matching structured clinical interview and infant-directed prosodic effect sizes (Cohen d ~ 0.50 - 0.65).
scenario_3_moderate_evidence_informed.physiological_bounds_plausibility: High physiological plausibility. Zero clamping. Variance of clinical covariate signal approximately equals residual noise variance (SNR ~ 1.0).
